metadata.title: Worries About OpenAI’s Revenue Rattle the AI Trade

content.text:
Key Takeaways
-
AI-related stocks sank Thursday in the wake of a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualized revenue might be lower than previously anticipated.
-
The discrepancy arose from investors' efforts to arrive at a number more directly comparable to Anthropic's figures, the FT reported.
Fears that OpenAI's revenue might be lower than expected are weighing on the AI trade.
Nvidia (NVDA), Oracle (ORCL), Arm (ARM), CoreWeave (CRWV), and other AI-related stocks were among the biggest decliners in the major indexes Thursday. The S&P 500 Information Technology Sector dropped 1.8%, making it the worst performer of the 11 industries tracked by the benchmark index.
The sharp decline follows a report by the Financial Times that OpenAI recently told investors its annualized revenues were approaching $50 billion at the end of September, well below the $70 billion figure the FT previously suggested.
The FT called the discrepancy, which came from investors' efforts to arrive at a number more directly comparable to Anthropic's figures, "a massive gap likely to damp optimism about the growth of AI demand." The report noted Anthropic, which is reportedly expected to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue this year, has typically included sales through cloud parters such as Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google in the metric, while OpenAI does not.
OpenAI did not respond to an Investopedia request for comment on the report in time for publication.
"The $20B gap between OpenAI's real run-rate and reported number is simply the value of sales flowing through [Amazon Web Services], Google and [Microsoft] Azure, but it's another great reminder of the winner of the AI model race keeps looking like whoever owns the distribution toll booth, which is Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta and Palantir," Shay Boloor, Chief Market Strategist at Futurum Equities, said in emailed comments.
